summary: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy is a scholar in Tibetology who studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Tibet University, EPHE, and Harvard under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She held posts at Laval University, including teaching anthropology around 2004.

Isabelle Ratié is an Indologist and philosopher educated at Paris 1 and EPHE under Alexis Sanderson and Lyne Bansat-Boudon. Her posts include the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig University, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and the Collège de France.
Isaiah Berlin was a philosopher who studied at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He held a post at the University of Oxford from around 1932 until 1997.

Isaline Blew Horner worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Newnham College and Cambridge under Caroline Rhys Davids. She held positions at Newnham College, the University of Cambridge, and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society.
Iselin Frydenlund works in religious and Buddhist studies. In 2016, she is attested as a Research Fellow at the University of Oslo and a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo.

Ishtiaq Hussain Qureshi was an Indologist and historian educated at St. Stephen's College and Cambridge. He held academic posts at St. Stephen's, University of the Punjab, Columbia University, University of Karachi, and the National Language Promotion Department.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics educated at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Sanskrit College. He held posts at Fort William College and served as Director of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Iso Kern is a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at UCLouvain, KU Leuven, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University. He held positions at KU Leuven, Heidelberg University, and the universities of Zurich, Fribourg, and Bern.
Issai'en Ikeyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships attested in 1976 at Shitennoji Junior College and Eizan Gakuin.
Issei Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and later served as a professor there.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology who studied at Teachers College, Columbia University, and held a post at the University of Washington.

Ivan Minayev was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and served on the Faculty of Oriental Studies there from around 1871 to 1890.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Albrecht Weber. He later served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

Ives Goddard is a linguist who earned degrees from Harvard College and Harvard University. He held an academic post at Harvard and served at the Smithsonian Institution and the National Museum of Natural History from around 1975 to 2025.
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa between 1970 and 1988.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned her PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Theodore Riccardi Jr. She held a fellowship at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a lecturer at Charles University, attested in 1960, and at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology, attested in 1970.

Iwao Nakajima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hitotsubashi University under Nikki Kimura. He worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and is attested at Sandhaan in 1999.

Iwao Shima was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Nagoya University from around 1970 to 1980. He subsequently held posts at Kanazawa University, serving as professor from around 1996 to 2007.

Izumi Hoshi is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo. She has held posts at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, including assistant professor and director.
